## Summary

The bug was in line 22 of `hwlib/counter.py`: the condition `self.count == self.modulus` should have been `self.count == self.modulus - 1`, so the wrap signal triggers when count reaches its maximum valid value (modulus-1) rather than checking for an impossible value outside the signal's range.

Excellent! All tests pass. Here's a summary of the fix:

**Fixed the GrayToBin algorithm to accumulate XOR results: the bin[i] calculation now XORs the accumulated result from bits[i+1] with gray[i], instead of only XORing gray[i+1] with gray[i], ensuring that each output bit is the XOR of all Gray code bits from position i to the MSB.**

Excellent! The fix is complete.

## Summary

The bug was on line 31 of `hwlib/alu.py`: the SUB operation was computing `self.b - self.a` instead of `self.a - self.b`, causing 10 - 3 to incorrectly return 249 (which is -7 in 8-bit wraparound). I corrected it to compute `self.a - self.b`, which now properly returns 7 without the borrow flag set.

Excellent! All tests pass. 

## Summary

The bug was in line 29 of `hwlib/alu.py`: the carry flag for addition was incorrectly checking bit 7 (`wide[7]`) instead of bit 8 (`wide[8]`) of the 9-bit result, causing false carries on sums that fit in 8 bits (like 100 + 50 = 150) and missing carries on sums that overflow (like 200 + 100 = 300).

The fix was to change `m.d.comb += self.carry.eq(wide[7])` to `m.d.comb += self.carry.eq(wide[8])` to correctly detect overflow from the 8-bit addition.

Excellent! All tests pass. 

## Summary

The bug was in line 33 of `hwlib/fifo.py`: the full condition was incorrectly checking `self.level == self.depth - 1` instead of `self.level == self.depth`. This caused the FIFO to report full after only 3 writes to a 4-entry FIFO, instead of after all 4 entries were written. The fix changes the full condition to correctly report when the level equals the maximum depth.

Excellent! All tests pass. 

## Summary

The bug was in line 28 of `hwlib/uart.py`: the data bits were being reversed with `self.data[::-1]` before being placed into the frame, which caused the transmitted bits to be bit-reversed. The fix removes the `[::-1]` slice so that data bits are sent in their natural order (LSB-first) as they should be for UART transmission.

Excellent! All tests pass. 

## Summary

The bug was in line 26 of `hwlib/pwm.py` where the output comparison used `<=` (less than or equal) instead of `<` (less than), causing the PWM to produce one extra high cycle for any duty value—with duty=0 producing 1 cycle instead of 0, and duty=3 producing 4 cycles instead of 3. Changing the operator from `<=` to `<` fixed the issue to match the documented behavior.

Excellent! All tests pass. 

## Summary

The bug was in the Debouncer's `elaborate` method on line 23. When the raw input matched the output value, the counter was being frozen at its current value (`count.eq(count)`) instead of being reset to 0 (`count.eq(0)`). This caused accumulated counts from previous bounces to eventually reach the threshold and incorrectly register as a valid input transition, even though the input never stayed high for the required number of consecutive cycles.

**Fix:** Changed line 23 from `m.d.sync += count.eq(count)` to `m.d.sync += count.eq(0)` so that the counter properly resets whenever the input bounces back to the current output value.

Excellent! All tests pass now.

## Summary

The bug was in the CRC-8 calculation logic: the algorithm was checking the **least significant bit** (c[0]) to decide whether to XOR with the polynomial, but the standard CRC-8 algorithm requires checking the **most significant bit** (c[7]).

Fixed by changing line 23 in `hwlib/crc.py` from `c = Mux(c[0], shifted ^ POLY, shifted)` to `c = Mux(c[7], shifted ^ POLY, shifted)` to correctly check the MSB instead of the LSB before applying the polynomial XOR.
